message.content:
Review: The problem is well differentiated from the target paper’s reported finding: rather than treating coarsening as an established cause, it proposes controlled interventions to test whether changing coarsening changes the onset or persistence of subharmonic order. The focus on synchronized repeated runs, run-level uncertainty, preregistered onset criteria, and drive-only and disorder controls gives the question a credible causal and methodological contribution. The supplied aggregate measurements motivate the question but cannot themselves answer it, since they lack temporal-order signals and independent run identifiers.

Feedback: The originality lies mainly in the causal test and the comparison of competing mechanisms, not in the general link between coarsening and time-crystalline order, which the target paper already reports. The proposed coupling intervention needs careful interpretation: changing coupling may affect temporal order directly as well as through coarsening, so it cannot isolate mediation on its own. Specify how coupling’s direct effects will be assessed, and define the temporal-order metric and its robustness to finite-window and drive-frequency choices before data collection. Also clarify whether the “first sustained threshold crossing” is estimated per run and how onset uncertainty and runs that never cross the threshold will be handled. These refinements would make the claimed mechanistic distinction more persuasive.

Rating (1-5): 4
